name: Sopova & Ford, eq. (15): planar plasma-model near-wall coefficient K = (sqrt2/(128 pi)) omega_p

source.located: arXiv:quant-ph/0504143v2 (9 Jun 2005), V. Sopova and L. H. Ford, 'The Electromagnetic Field Stress Tensor between Dielectric Half-Spaces', Sec. III, eq. (15), p. 7; eq. (15) restates, halved, eq. (37) of the same authors' arXiv:quant-ph/0204125 (PRD 66, 045026 (2002)), which was also read
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content fullText=true (quant-ph/0504143, whole paper); answer_pdf_queries on quant-ph/0204125 (pp. 1-17, incl. eqs. 31-38 and Sec. 3.4)

published_statement: quant-ph/0504143 eq. (15): 'the asymptotic form of T_xx near the boundary z = 0 is one half the corresponding expression for U in this limit, which was found in Ref. [14]:  T_xx ~ (1/2) U ~ (sqrt2 omega_p/(128 pi)) (1/z^3), as z -> 0.'  Units: Lorentz-Heaviside, hbar = c = 1.  The origin, quant-ph/0204125 eq. (37): 'U ~ (sqrt2 omega_p/(64 pi)) (1/z^3)', with <E^2> ~ sqrt2 omega_p/(32 pi z^3) and <B^2> ~ -5 omega_p^2/(96 pi z^2) (eq. 38).  So sqrt2/(128 pi) is the coefficient of the TRANSVERSE pressure T_xx; U's is twice it.  In the same paper T_zz (normal pressure) is exactly z-independent (eq. 13): the planar normal stress does not diverge at all.
published_hypotheses: H1 planar geometry: vacuum gap 0<z<a between two half-spaces; eq. (15) is the z -> 0 (z << a) limit, where the position-dependent term dominates and reduces to the single-interface result

H2 collisionless plasma model eps(omega) = 1 - omega_p^2/omega^2 (no damping); 0204125 concl.: 'collisionless Drude model ... generic form ... at high frequencies ... should lead to the same limiting forms near an interface'

H3 SHARP (step) boundary between dielectric and vacuum; 0504143 p.7: 'this singular behavior ... can be viewed as due to the assumption of a sharp boundary at z = 0'; 0204125 Sec. 3.4: 'The divergence of U is not considered to be physical'
H4 zero temperature (eq. 15 is the T = 0 expression; finite-T enters only through Eqs. 9-12, 23-24)
H5 asymptotic regime omega_p z << 1 (leading term of a Taylor expansion in 1/u, 0204125 Sec. 3.4)
H6 non-magnetic media (mu = 1), isotropic, homogeneous, local (no spatial dispersion)
H7 Schwinger-DeRaad-Milton source-theory Green's-function formalism; renormalised by subtracting the empty-space (no-wall) term
hypothesis_drift: COMPONENT UNNAMED (not an error): tolman.py:1138-1140 calls sqrt2/(128 pi) 'the coefficient of omega_p in K' and tolman.py:1517-1521 writes 'K = K_SF omega_p' without saying K is the TRANSVERSE-pressure coefficient. The tree's p_r^real ~ K/(a eps^2) is consistent only with p_t = K/eps^3 (checked, rederive 6a); had K been read from U the crossover would be 0.2400843510, not 0.4801687020 (rederive 5). The tree's use is the correct component; the drift is that the component is not written into the claim.

DROPPED H3 (sharp boundary): no site in tolman.py names it (grep 'sharp' finds only Misner-Sharp). The source names the step boundary as the CAUSE of the 1/z^3 divergence and calls it unphysical; Parashar-Milton et al. 1804.04045 Sec. VI B show that with the plasma model and a continuous permittivity the normal-normal edge singularity disappears. The crossover a_c (tolman.py:1524-1527) compares two near-wall asymptotics and inherits H3.

DROPPED H5 as a named scale: the statement's 'near-wall' (canonical hypotheses) does not name omega_p eps/c << 1. Measured here: the leading term is 10.9 % off at omega_p z = 0.1, 1.2 % at 0.01, 0.12 % at 0.001 (rederive 3). With a_c = 0.480 lambdabar_p, the comparison lives at eps << lambdabar_p AND eps << a ~ 0.48 lambdabar_p (gold: eps << ~10 nm).
DROPPED H4 (T = 0): not named in tolman.py (grep 'temperature' empty). Harmless at the near-wall scale (the source: thermal effects negligible for distances << 1/kT), recorded for completeness.

WIDENED H2 to 'EVERY CONDUCTOR': tolman.py:1525, 3041-3042 and 3265 state a_c = 0.480 x skin depth 'FOR EVERY CONDUCTOR', and tolman.py:3048-3051 checks 'the material-independence is exact' by evaluating the SAME plasma-model formula at two omega_p values (a CONSTRUCTION, tautological within H2). Re-derived here for general eps(i zeta): U ~ I/(16 pi^2 z^3), T_xx ~ I/(32 pi^2 z^3), I = INT_0^inf dzeta (eps(i zeta)-1)/(eps(i zeta)+1); the plasma model gives I = pi omega_p/(2 sqrt2) (rederive 1a-1d). The single-scale universality is a property of the collisionless plasma model, not of conductors: Drude damping moves K by -0.17 % (9.0 eV/35 meV) to -0.28 % (7.84 eV/49 meV) (rederive 4); interband structure of a real metal (gold interband onset ~2.45 eV per 0801.1384, below omega_p) enters I and is NOT computed here. The canonical hypothesis list keeps 'plasma model conductor', so the claim holds for every PLASMA-MODEL conductor.

PLANAR -> SPHERE: tolman.py:1057-1060 marks the curvature extension RECONSTRUCTED, sign and order only -- acknowledged by the tree, not a drift. Evidence gathered: the conservation step p_t = C/eps^n -> p_r reproduces Li 2411.07911's explicit spherical computation (2/3 ratio, same sign) in the NON-dispersive case (rederive 6b-6c); no explicit spherical plasma-model computation was found (Li 2024 states it does not include dispersion).

STATUS: tolman.py:1138-1140 and 2537-2538 carry 'RECOVERED via DOCKET 54's verbatim quotation; not re-read at source'. Read at source here: the quotation matches eq. (15) verbatim in content; no transcription discrepancy found.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0). (1) Closed-form sympy: the near-wall limit of the one-interface U (0204125 eq. 35) for GENERAL eps is I/(16 pi^2 z^3); plasma I = sqrt2 pi omega_p/4 = pi omega_p/(2 sqrt2), so U z^3 -> sqrt2 omega_p/(64 pi) and T_xx z^3 -> sqrt2 omega_p/(128 pi): eq. (15) reproduced exactly. (2) sympy: in the one-wall limit the eq. (14) integrand is exactly half the eq. (8) integrand. (3) Numeric quadrature of the EXACT one-interface integral: z^3 U/omega_p / (sqrt2/(64 pi)) = 0.89110, 0.98812, 0.99880, 0.99988, 0.99998800 at omega_p z = 1e-1 ... 1e-5, monotone convergence (relative deviation 1.2e-5 at 1e-5); the O(z^-2) subleading slope -0.00844 is of the size of 0204125 eq. (38b)'s -5/(192 pi) = -0.00829 contribution. (4) Drude damping shifts K by -0.17 % to -0.28 % for gold parameters. (5) K_SF/A_EM = 60 sqrt2 pi/128 = 2.0826013773, a_c/lambdabar_p = 0.4801687020, gold a_c 10.5278 nm, aluminium 6.19283 nm -- all the tree's pins reproduced; the U-coefficient misreading would give 0.2400843510. (6) sympy: p_t = K/eps^3 with the spherical conservation law gives p_r = K/(a eps^2) (the tree's form); the same step at n = 4 gives 2/3, matching Li 2411.07911 eqs. (38a,b) explicitly.

later_literature.what: The origin of eq. (15): U ~ sqrt2 omega_p/(64 pi z^3) (eq. 37), with the mechanism -- the TM coefficient r' -> 1 at grazing incidence -- and the explicit caveat that the divergence reflects the idealised smooth sharp surface and is not considered physical.

later_literature.ref: Yang Li, arXiv:2411.07911 (2024), 'Casimir stresses of the dielectric ball: inhomogeneity and divergences'
later_literature.what: For a spherical ball the leading near-surface stresses equal the planar ones (radial ZERO, transverse ~ q^-4), and the spherical geometry adds an O(a^-1 z^-3) radial term; eqs. (38a,b) give T_rr/T_tt coefficients in the ratio 2/3 that the conservation step reproduces. Non-dispersive only ('we will not take the dispersion into account'), so the plasma-sphere prefactor the tree RECONSTRUCTS is not computed there either.

later_literature.ref: Parashar, Milton, Li, Day, Guo, Fulling, Cavero-Pelaez, arXiv:1804.04045 (2018)
later_literature.what: Edge singularities of the planar EM stress tensor are universal but fixed by the structure of the permittivity discontinuity (1/z^3 in T_zz for a step with a slope scale, 1/z^2 for a slope discontinuity only); with the plasma model and continuous permittivity the normal-normal edge singularity disappears. The near-wall coefficient therefore depends on H3, which the tree does not name.

later_literature.ref: Svetovoy, van Zwol, Palasantzas, De Hosson, arXiv:0801.1384 (2008)
later_literature.what: Measured gold-film plasma frequencies 6.8-8.4 eV against the community's 9.0 eV, damping 35-49 meV; film eps(i zeta) differs from the reference by > 15 % near 1 eV. Supplies the data that move the tree's nm pins and show the 'every conductor' universality is plasma-model only.

lacked_data: What Sopova & Ford (2002/2005) lacked: any measured optical data -- they used a one-parameter collisionless plasma model and no sample eps(omega); nor had the near-surface literature on smooth permittivity profiles (Griniasty-Leonhardt; Parashar-Milton et al. 2018) or explicit spherical computations (Li 2024) appeared. What came later and what it does, computed here: (a) measured omega_p (6.8-8.4 eV films vs 9.0 eV): eq. (15) is stated in units of omega_p, so the coefficient sqrt2/(128 pi) and the tree's a_c/lambdabar_p = 0.480 are untouched; only the nm pins move (gold a_c 10.53 -> 11.31-13.89 nm). (b) measured damping: K moves by -0.17 % to -0.28 % (computed). (c) real interband eps(i zeta): changes the material integral I and therefore the coefficient for a real metal -- not computable here (OPEN). (d) smooth-boundary theory: the authors already named the sharp boundary as the source of the divergence, so this is not data they lacked but an idealisation they flagged. Net: evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result -- no later datum refutes eq. (15) within its stated hypotheses, and the re-derivation reproduces it exactly; the limits that matter (H3, and the plasma model standing in for 'every conductor') were named by the source or are model scope, not missing data.
grade_evidence: The coefficient itself STANDS: read at source (eq. 15, and its origin 0204125 eq. 37), re-derived in closed form for general eps(i zeta) and specialised to the plasma model (sympy), and confirmed numerically on the exact integral to 1.2e-5 at omega_p z = 1e-5; the tree's arithmetic (2.0826013773, 0.4801687020, 10.5278 nm, 6.19283 nm) reproduces, and the tree uses the correct (transverse) component. It is NARROWED against the tree's use because (i) the tree drops the sharp-boundary hypothesis the source names as the cause of the 1/z^3 singularity (and 1804.04045 shows plasma-model edge singularities vanish for continuous profiles), (ii) the tree never names the scale omega_p eps/c << 1 (leading term 11 % off at 0.1), and (iii) tolman.py:1525/3041/3265 widen the plasma-model material-independence to 'EVERY CONDUCTOR', while for a general eps(i zeta) K = I/(32 pi^2) with I material-dependent (Drude damping alone -0.17 to -0.28 %, computed; interband OPEN). Not WRONG: no counterexample to eq. (15) within its hypotheses exists here. Not DATA-DEPENDENT for the ratio: omega_p cancels; the moved omega_p only shifts nm pins.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree writes H3 (sharp step boundary), the scale omega_p eps/c << 1 and T = 0 into the claim, names K as the transverse-pressure coefficient, and scopes 'FOR EVERY CONDUCTOR' to 'for every collisionless-plasma-model conductor'. Toward DATA-DEPENDENT: a computation of I = INT (eps-1)/(eps+1) dzeta from tabulated gold/aluminium eps(i zeta) showing a_c/lambdabar_p differs materially from 0.480 for real metals (not run here: no tabulated data held). Toward WRONG: only a computed counterexample to eq. (15) within H1-H7, which the exact numeric integral here rules out.
